_doc: Jaipur (Nagar Nigam Jaipur) upstream sources for Headwaters. Every artifact Jaipur ships names its upstreams by id, with the artifact in that id's dependsOn.

Platform-wide upstreams stay under their existing ids and carry Jaipur's paths in their dependsOn rather than being duplicated: OpenStreetMap, Open-Meteo, FABDEM and the CPCB reports in platform.json.

sources.license: IMD data policy; gridded rainfall retrieved programmatically via imdlib, cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: cron .github/workflows/imd-rainfall-refresh.yml (neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/generate_imd_rainfall.py --city jaipur); first generated on the laptop with uv run --no-project --with imdlib --with xarray --with numpy --with pandas
sources.notes: Cell 26.75 N / 75.75 E contains IMD's Jaipur (Sanganer) observatory, station 42348. Checked 2026-10-20: the cell's 1991-2020 mean is 591.9 mm against the observatory's 1991-2020 normal of 600.3 mm (IMD Climatological Tables 1991-2020, printed p.166), -1.4%; every year 1991-2020 within 0.75-1.27x of the Rajasthan SW manual gauge at Sanganer (NWDP, one value per day). No zero or missing year 1970-2025.

sources.refreshMethod: manual: each January's Annual Progress Report (pragati vivaranika); update src/cities/jaipur/commitments.json and the supply and facts builders' figures with their pages
sources.notes: PHED runs Jaipur's water supply (Bisalpur transmission, Surajpura treatment, city distribution, 3,633 tube wells). The Annual Progress Reports 2024-25 (January 2025) and 2025-26 (January 2026) give, per city project, sanction, work order, spend, percent done and target date; the 2025-26 report's Jaipur city row (status 31.12.2025, printed p.85 / PDF p.89) gives 766.73 MLD, 590 from Bisalpur. Hindi in the legacy Kruti Dev font: the text layer is unreadable, read figures from page images. Site copyright page: 'Material featured on this site may be reproduced free of charge in any format or media without requiring specific permission ... the source must be prominently acknowledged.'

sources.license: Government of Rajasthan publication, cited with attribution
sources.cadence: daily (mid-June to mid-October); 1st and 16th of the month otherwise, posted late
sources.refreshMethod: neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/scrape_rajasthan_wrd_dams.py --cache <dir> --artifact --supabase, then --backfill-from 7 days back (local scheduled job; the list API and PDFs are on the Rajasthan state data centre). History: --backfill-from 2023-06-16, 2026-10-21.
sources.notes: 'Water Storage Data' PDFs (Details of Large, Medium & Small Dams of Rajasthan State), listed by the portal's own POST API on medicalportal.rajasthan.gov.in and served from jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in. % is present gross volume over designed (gross) capacity, not live storage: never splice with CWC's live-storage %. Terms & Conditions: 'Though all efforts have been made to ensure the accuracy and currency of the content on this website, the same should not be construed as a statement of law or used for any legal purposes.' No reuse licence stated; wrd.rajasthan.gov.in does not resolve (2026-10-20). The 05.08.2025 storage file answers 404 (read from that day's bulletin); 2023 bulletins print the dam tables in Kruti Dev; the Chhaparwara row of 18.06.2026 misprints Kalakhsagar's figures and is withheld; Ramsagar Newta prints gauge 0.00 from June 2025 to June 2026; the Jaipur-row Chandlai storage never leaves 1.99-2.04 Mcum.

sources.license: no explicit licence: the IN-GRES portal publishes no terms of use, no disclaimer and no copyright or licence statement anywhere; nothing has been established about who may redistribute this material or on what terms
sources.refreshMethod: neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/build_ingres_gwr.py --city jaipur (also writes the unit polygons from the IN-GRES GeoServer)
sources.notes: Dynamic Ground Water Resources for Jaipur district drilled to its 16 assessment units, five editions from 2021-2022. IN-GRES is ONE upstream serving every state; this entry is the Rajasthan cut. Rajasthan's state UUID came from the COUNTRY-level API call. IN-GRES still serves the 33 pre-2023 districts. The 2024-2025 district figures equal Rajasthan's printed Dynamic Ground Water Resources 2025 (printed p.168). Jaipur Urban's 2022-2023 row equals the state's GWRA 2023 report (printed p.49).

sources.publisher: National Water Informatics Centre (NWIC), Ministry of Jal Shakti
sources.license: Government of India open data portal: its copyright policy permits reproduction free of charge in any format without specific permission, reproduced accurately and with the source prominently acknowledged; cited with attribution
sources.notes: Rajasthan groundwater-level telemetry on the CKAN portal: Rajasthan Ground Water Department six-hourly resources 2fe60c40-217d-43da-8927-d881c80d17d4 (2021-2025) and f33c4e60-7dbf-4b15-802a-ec8737cdd319 (2026-2030), and CGWB telemetry 467fe983-e1f0-4428-91b7-0ade87b39f6d and 931ff862-f13e-4754-83f9-55e0dc894f2d. TRAPS: the District tag is upper case ('JAIPUR') and follows pre-2023 lines; 999.0 is the state series' placeholder; zeros and sign flips occur; Durgapura_1 (about 8 m) is not CGWB's 100 m Durgapura piezometer; Jaisingpur Khor_1 steps from about 56 m to 3 m; about 70 state wells report only from 27 Jul to 3 Sep 2026. Shallow and deep piezometers stand side by side (Durgapura about 8 m, Mansarovar about 42 m).

sources.notes: LSG notification P.10(N.Pa.)(Gathan)(Chunav)DLB/25/19631 of 16 Sep 2025 (Rajasthan Municipalities Act 2009 ss.3, 10), Rajasthan Gazette Extraordinary Part 6(A), 20 Sep 2025: 150 wards with population (sum 3,197,135; census basis not stated). PDF on jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in, byte-identical on jaipurmc.org as FinalParisimanGazette2025.pdf. LSG page is an Angular app; list via webapi/PublicPortal/DepartmentPages/GetDepartmentPageDetail?deptCode=371474&lookupCode=0&pageCode=2380. Devanagari text layer broken: ward 116 (24,725) read from page image p.52. Text boundaries only, no geometry.

Administrative Directory https://jaipurmc.org/PDF/Others/jp_AdminContList.pdf (Kruti Dev; read from page images): zone office lines and emails. Zone spellings from the Jaipur Samadhan zone list. Officer mobiles, councillor names and parties never used. Terms: 'may be reproduced free of charge ... the source must be prominently acknowledged.'

sources.notes: Ex-post evaluation of the Bisalpur-Jaipur Water Supply Project (Transfer System): 120 km from Jaipur (p.3); 97% groundwater of 345,000 m3/day at appraisal in 2003, 18.8% in 2015 (pp.2, 18-19); intake 396,000 m3/day in 2015 (Table 6, p.18); NRW 37% in 2015 with 45-81% of meters out of order in four zones (p.18); built March 2004 - May 2013 (Table 4, p.15).
